title: Resolving the Dark Matter Inverse Problem: Physics-Informed Neural Networks for High-Precision Spectral Reconstruction
content: The indirect detection of dark matter through gamma-ray emission from dwarf spheroidal galaxies (dSphs) provides a promising avenue for probing the particle nature of dark matter. However, extracting dark matter parameters from gamma-ray spectra remains a challenging inverse problem, particularly when conventional statistical and computational methods require repeated evaluations of physical models over a large parameter space. In this study, we develop a Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN) in an inverse configuration to infer key dark matter properties, including the particle mass and velocity-averaged annihilation cross section, from gamma-ray spectral data associated with dSphs. The proposed framework incorporates the underlying dark matter annihilation flux equation directly into the learning process, allowing the network to exploit both observational information and physical constraints. This physics-informed formulation enables the model to establish a physically consistent mapping between gamma-ray spectra and the corresponding dark matter parameters. The proposed PINN achieves a low spectral reconstruction error, with a Mean Squared Error (MSE) of 1.7×10-3, while providing a computationally efficient alternative to conventional parameter-inference approaches. These results demonstrate the potential of PINNs for accelerating inverse dark matter analyses and establishing efficient surrogate models for gamma-ray-based indirect detection. The framework provides a foundation for extending physics-informed machine learning to more realistic observational datasets and broader dark matter parameter spaces.
